study: run-length axis at the certified Ma and dt (closes the ma_envelope open item; out-of-sample test of Psi)

declared_points.role: the run named by the Ma-envelope open item: run length doubled at the certified Ma and dt
out-of-sample Psi point: predicted fail if the accumulated index, and not Ma, sets the boundary
Psi extrapolation, 2.2x beyond the in-sample failing point

evidence.dt_candidate_statement: P3 and P4 share dt = 3.250e-04 s (2.00x the certified dt) and differ only in run length (1 s vs 2 s); P3 passes every gate and P4 fails profile RMS and wall shear. A doubled dt is therefore not sufficient to break the band: within this pair the discriminating variable is the run length (Psi 18.0 -> 32.9).
evidence.still_open: The same run length has never been run at the *certified* Ma and dt, so the failure cannot yet be attributed to accumulated time alone rather than to the higher Ma; that is exactly point T1 (t_end = 2.0 s, c_s = 20), which this module declares and grades.

in_sample_band.open_item: Two candidates survive and are not separated by the present sweep: (i) Ma-dependent growth of particle disorder, (ii) the doubled dt that comes with the lowered c_s (P3/P4 run at dt = 3.25e-4 vs 1.63e-4 for P0). The discriminating run is c_s = 20 with t_end = 2.0 (twenty-three thousand steps, ~160 s), which does not fit the 120 s local execution cap; a cluster submission sat queued >30 min without dispatch and was abandoned. Until that run exists, the Psi index must not be quoted as a stability criterion.

verdict.statement: None of the declared run-length points has an artifact on disk, so this study makes no claim about the run-length axis. What the committed seven-point sweep already settles is recorded separately in existing_evidence(): the doubled-dt candidate is eliminated as a sufficient cause, and the certified-Ma long run (T1) remains the missing discriminator.
